messages.subject: comparison of e.g. data set with two or more categories
parts:
Hi.

What statistical analyses are advisable to perfom on e.g. line transect data where missing datapoints are present.

If you have a set -uo with two treatments and a control that you persom line transects throught to detect in a sertain speceis is present in the transect and you measure the perp dist if the species is present. But in some of the transects no speciment is found and thus NA is noted in that transect.

What statistical analyses could be used?

best regards,

Nicolai

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] comparison of e.g. data set with two or more categories
parts:
Nicolai:

The absence of sightings on a transect is not equivalent to "NA" the lack of sightings is itself information, so do not consider that as "missing data".  The transect was walked (or flown, ...) and nothing was sighted.  The amount of survey effort associated with the transect needs to be recorded as part of your survey protocol.

For valid inference, your control and two treatment areas should have replicate transects placed in them.  Hopefully there is sufficient replication such that you can produce density estimates (and measures of precision) for each of the 3 areas being investigated.  If so, then section 3.6.5 of Buckland et al. (2001) can provide guidance on making comparisons of density estimates.
